title: The second vector on the pair of solutions, and the co-distance-3 cancellation
claim: Pre-registered 2026-11-10, before the proof attempt. At n = 2^m, h = n/2, q = 2n, for a in GF(q)* with G the monic least-degree element of ker X_b, k = h - deg G >= 3, J = ceil(k/2), e = h - J - 1, G' the second solution of LEADING-FORM-20261110-001A (W(G, G') = c Y^e) and the family Zhat of CHAIN-ORDERS-20261110-001A: to be proved (1) the second vector of the reduction is, modulo the kernel, psi_2(x) = [What_x G + W_x G']/(c Y^e) with W_x = W(G, psi_2(x)) and What_x the polynomial in Y of degree below e congruent to W_x G'/G mod k^e; target (2), the co-distance-3 cancellation: with a complement containing k G Y^j (2j < k - 1), the reduction's coefficients at l^4 and l^5 vanish on every entry with i + j <= k - 3; then there is no Jordan block of size 4, exactly one of size 5 when k is odd and none when k is even, and the chain lemma holds in full for k <= 3. Frozen stop rule: if (2) is not derived in this epic, the collapse line is parked.
failure_conditions: An eigenvalue and an entry with i + j <= k - 3 at which the reduction's coefficient at l^4 or l^5 is nonzero (computed false at every a for sides 8 to 256).
remaining_obligations: (1) and (2), or the record of what failed
foundation_claim_scope: The square torus of rule-60 rings with equally spaced law-(12, 12) contacts, cut open by a ring of cuts each way (A30, A32, A37, A38); its walk over GF(2), at sides 2^m. The spectrum is a contact-level reading, so it does not depend on how the rings are declared (A45).

validation.status: pre-registered; the proof attempt to follow
